questions.question: A quotation uses a source’s words in what form?
choices: a new sentence with the same idea
a summary of a whole chapter
the exact wording, marked as borrowed
an uncited statement

questions.question: A paraphrase restates a source’s idea using what?
choices: the writer’s own wording and sentence structure
the source’s exact sentence
only a few swapped synonyms
an unattributed quotation

questions.question: A summary presents what?
choices: every source detail in order
an exact sentence
the writer’s opinion only
the main points in a shorter form

questions.question: Attribution tells readers what?
choices: how long the essay is
whose idea or words are being used
which paragraph is longest
where the writer sat

questions.question: Why should a direct quotation be placed in quotation marks?
choices: to make the source claim more reliable
to show the exact words come from another source
to replace a citation
to indicate the writer disagrees

questions.question: A student copies a sentence and changes two words without quotation marks. What is the problem?
choices: the student has written a summary
the citation is automatically complete
the sentence is a paraphrase
the wording remains too close to the source and is unattributed

questions.question: Which paraphrase is strongest?
choices: it accurately restates the idea in new wording and cites the source
it replaces a few words with synonyms
it keeps the source’s sentence structure and removes quotation marks
it changes the source’s meaning

questions.question: A writer quotes one sentence but leaves out a phrase that changes its meaning. What is the ethical concern?
choices: the quotation is too short
the source is secondary
the quotation misrepresents the source
quotation marks are unnecessary

questions.question: A paraphrase still requires what?
choices: attribution to the original source
quotation marks around every word
no citation because wording changed
a new author name

questions.question: A writer introduces a quotation with the source’s name and context. What does this help readers understand?
choices: that the quote needs no explanation
that the source is always correct
who said it and why it is relevant
that the writer agrees with every detail

questions.question: Which sentence integrates a quotation and attribution clearly?
choices: “Public spaces invite shared responsibility.”
Lee argues, “Public spaces invite shared responsibility.”
Lee says, “public spaces invite shared responsibility,” and that is true.
The source says public spaces, shared responsibility.

questions.question: A student’s paragraph contains a long quotation but little explanation. What should revision add?
choices: more copied sentences
fewer citations
an unrelated summary
analysis connecting the quoted evidence to the claim

questions.question: A writer needs a brief factual detail from a source. What approach is often best?
choices: copy the sentence without quotation marks
omit attribution
present it as personal knowledge
paraphrase the detail and cite it

questions.question: A source uses an unusual phrase that is central to the analysis. What is an appropriate way to preserve it?
choices: change one word and omit attribution
quote the exact phrase and attribute it
copy the full paragraph
place it in italics without a citation

questions.question: A student paraphrases a source but changes “may increase” to “always causes.” What is the issue?
choices: the paraphrase is too concise
the source becomes primary
the paraphrase exaggerates the source’s claim
the writer has added a citation

questions.question: A citation appears after a paragraph with ideas from two sources, but readers cannot tell which idea came from whom. What is needed?
choices: clearer attribution near each borrowed idea
a longer title
fewer transitions
more quotation marks around original writing

questions.question: When is a direct quotation especially useful?
choices: whenever a source has a sentence
when the exact wording matters to the analysis
when the writer has no claim
when a source is difficult to understand

questions.question: A writer uses a source’s idea and adds their own interpretation. What should the writer do?
choices: present both as the source’s exact words
remove the citation
distinguish the source’s contribution from their analysis
cite only the writer’s own idea

questions.question: A student cites a source in a bibliography but copies a sentence in the essay without quotation marks. What is still missing?
choices: a signal in the text marking the exact borrowed words
a second bibliography
the source’s title in every sentence
a summary of the citation style

questions.question: Which practice best avoids plagiarism while using research?
choices: copy passages into a draft and add citations later from memory
change a few words in every sentence
cite only sources that are quoted directly
take notes that distinguish exact quotations from paraphrases and record source details
